source_text: Oratio in inscriptione psalmorum graduum (fragmenta) Ο ΛΟΓΟΣ ΕΙΣ ΤΑΣ ΕΠΙΓΡΑΦΑΣ ΤΩΝ ΑΝΑΒΑΘΜΩΝ 33 ∆όξαν δὲ ἐπίκτητον ὁ Πατὴρ οὐκ ἐπιδέχεται, τέλειος, ἄπειρος, ἀπερινόητος ὢν, ἀπροσδεὴς κάλλους καὶ παντοίας εὐπρεπείας.
thought_title: The Father does not receive acquired glory
orientation: The author is beginning his explanation of why acquired glory is not fitting for the Father, stating the first reason in a series that will also cover the Word and the man of Christ.
pass_a_gloss: But acquired glory the Father does not receive, being perfect, infinite, incomprehensible, without need of beauty or seemliness.

choices.why: The glossary mandates 'acquired glory' for δόξαν ἐπίκτητον; the δέ is rendered as 'But' to mark the contrast with what precedes.
The verb means to admit or accept something offered; 'receive' keeps the sense of taking in what is external, matching the acquired nature of the glory.

choices.english: without need of beauty and of every kind of seemliness
choices.why: ἀπροσδεής takes a genitive of what is not needed; the repetition of 'of' preserves the two coordinated genitives clearly.
rejected: lacking need for beauty and all seemliness
in need of nothing, neither beauty nor any seemliness

choices.why: παντοίας means 'of every kind' or 'of all sorts'; 'seemliness' renders εὐπρέπεια as fittingness or comeliness, distinct from κάλλος (beauty).

pass_b_english: But the Father does not receive acquired glory, for he is perfect, infinite, incomprehensible, and without need of beauty and every kind of seemliness.
